steps.name: Stage-1 full range-test registration (rng1_r)
steps.content: Compute the documented old stage-1 form at the stage-1 cycle: hdist1 = s1_pos_r - hent_pos; rng1 = (hent_pos < s1_pos_r) && (hdist1 <= MAX_DIST) && (s1_pos_r < lim2). Register it as rng1_r aligned with hb_r <= s1_bytes (unconditional; consumption is gated by s1_vld_r). ERAM clk2q then drives only the flop D, same class as the existing hb_r path.
steps.rtl_refs: a1_deflate_core.v: hent_pos/hp_r (line ~1120), s1_ok (491), stage-1 register block (1118-1126), old stage-1 form comment (495-502)

steps.name: Stage 2 becomes flop-only for the range test
steps.content: Replace rng2 = (hp_r < pos) && (hdist2 <= MAX_DIST) && (pos < lim2) with rng2 = rng1_r; hit2 = s1_vld_r && hb_r && rng1_r (all flops). Keep hp_r / hdist2 / pos for the hit-branch data (cand_pos <= hp_r, dist_r <= hdist2) unchanged.

steps.name: Optional address precompute (only if post-split synth shows it critical)
steps.content: Precompute p3p1_r <= p3_r + 13'd1 (and reuse the existing hf1_r) so the hit-cycle bm_raddr_a branch is a flop value; update p3p1_r at every p3_r update site; record. At most this one address precompute.
steps.condition: only if the post-step-2 synth report shows the p3_r+1 adder -> ERAM mux path as critical

steps.name: Optional second predicate registration (only if post-split synth shows it critical)
steps.content: If a pos/lim2/blk_n comparator (e.g., pos < blk_n in cp_en, line 749) remains critical, register the corresponding stage-1 predicate (e.g., s1_blkn_r <= (s1_pos_r < blk_n)) and use it only where the documented pos == s1_pos_r(previous stage-1 cycle) relation holds; no FSM change, no cycle change; record. Limit: at most one additional registered predicate; no third pipeline stage anywhere.
steps.condition: only if synth after steps 1-2 (and 3) shows a pos/lim2/blk_n comparator still critical

design_notes: The equivalence (stage-2 pos == stage-1 s1_pos_r of the previous cycle; lim2 block-constant) is documented in the RTL comment (495-502) and must be proven by the 33-case regression.

If the stage-1 rng1 cone itself cannot meet timing, the attempt fails; a third pipeline stage is not allowed (it would add per-position cycles and break the throughput budget).
